notes.Scottie Barnes: Kawhi Leonard and RJ Barrett are both out again, so Toronto's offense runs through Barnes against Milwaukee; he played 37 minutes Friday in his second game back from a groin strain. Collin Murray-Boyles is probable to return from the concussion protocol, which helps the frontcourt but does not cut into Barnes' role.
notes.Shai Gilgeous-Alexander: Gilgeous-Alexander missed Sunday at Miami with a neck strain and a lower back contusion, his first absence of the season, and Oklahoma City had not filed today's injury report this morning, so his status at Indiana is not posted. If he plays on this thin roster, he is the offense; the Thunder dressed only nine players Sunday.
notes.Deni Avdija: Avdija came back from a foot contusion Saturday and played 36 minutes, and Ja Morant, Shaedon Sharpe and Vit Krejci are all still out for Portland. He is not on today's injury report, so he stays the Blazers' main creator at Philadelphia.
notes.Ty Jerome: Jerome returned Saturday from three games out with hip soreness and started for 27 minutes. Memphis is without Cameron Boozer, Jerami Grant, GG Jackson and Scotty Pippen Jr. at Charlotte, so there is room for his minutes to climb back toward 30.
notes.Devin Booker: Phoenix has spread its minutes across the bench lately, but Booker is the exception at 37 and 38 minutes in two of his last three games. Mark Williams is out after shoulder surgery and New Orleans is without Dejounte Murray and Bennedict Mathurin, while Zion Williamson is probable.
notes.Taylor Hendricks: Hendricks played 27 minutes off the bench Saturday with Cameron Boozer out, his most since 29 on November 14, and Boozer and Jerami Grant are both out again tonight. His minutes have swung from 11 to 29 this month, so he is a frontcourt fill-in rather than a locked-in starter.
notes.Buddy Hield: Hield started Sunday with Norman Powell (hamstring) and Caleb Wilson (fractured hand) out, played 40 minutes in overtime and was on the floor at the finish. Chicago is on the second night of a back-to-back against Cleveland and had not filed today's report this morning, so Powell's status is not posted.
notes.Danny Wolf: Wolf moved into the starting lineup Friday when Egor Demin went to the bench and played 26 minutes. Nolan Traore hurt his hamstring in that game and is out tonight, which keeps a starting spot open, but Brooklyn has not said who starts at Minnesota.
notes.Sion James: Kon Knueppel, Dennis Schroder and Grayson Allen (concussion protocol) are all out for Charlotte, and James started Friday and played 32 minutes. Brandon Miller is probable, so James stays in a starter's role as a defender and spot-up shooter.
notes.Jaylen Wells: Wells has started each of Memphis' recent games at 24 to 27 minutes, and the Grizzlies are without Cameron Boozer, Jerami Grant, GG Jackson and Scotty Pippen Jr. at Charlotte. Ty Jerome's return Saturday pushed Cam Spencer to the bench, not Wells.
notes.Allen Graves: Graves started Friday with Collin Murray-Boyles in the concussion protocol and played 33 minutes, but Murray-Boyles is probable tonight. Before that injury Graves played 13 to 16 minutes off the bench, so his role likely shrinks with Murray-Boyles back.
notes.Oso Ighodaro: Ighodaro has started every Phoenix game in our box scores since November 10, playing 17 to 33 minutes, and Mark Williams is out after shoulder surgery. His value comes from defense and rebounds rather than scoring.
notes.Royce O'Neale: O'Neale played 34 minutes the last time Grayson Allen sat (November 17), and Allen is out again in the concussion protocol along with Kon Knueppel and Dennis Schroder. That leaves Charlotte short on wings and opens bench minutes for him.
notes.Brandon Ingram: Ingram is off the Clippers' injury report and set for his season debut at Houston after right heel surgery. A minutes limit is possible in his first game, and his return takes wing shots from Keaton Wagler and the rest of the bench, with Bradley Beal out.
notes.Jaylen Brown: Brown is probable against Portland after missing every game since November 16 with a left hamstring strain. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, who started both games Brown missed, is expected to go back to the bench.
notes.Kentavious Caldwell-Pope: Caldwell-Pope started both games Jaylen Brown missed and played 32 and 35 minutes, but Brown is probable tonight, so Caldwell-Pope is expected back in a bench role.
notes.Zion Williamson: Williamson is probable against Phoenix with a thigh contusion after sitting Saturday, and Trey Murphy III is also probable. He played 37 minutes in his last game on Friday.
notes.Derik Queen: Queen started Saturday and played 35 minutes with Zion Williamson and Trey Murphy III sitting, but both are probable tonight. Before that he had slid to 18 and 19 minutes off the bench, so his role likely shrinks.
notes.Victor Wembanyama: Wembanyama is questionable at Sacramento, and De'Aaron Fox is questionable with a shin contusion; San Antonio is already without Dylan Harper and Tobias Harris. He played only 32 minutes Saturday because the Spurs led by 26 late.
notes.De'Aaron Fox: Fox is questionable at Sacramento with a right shin contusion, and Dylan Harper is still out, so if Fox sits the Spurs are thin at guard. Victor Wembanyama is also questionable.
notes.Josh Giddey: Giddey was benched in the fourth quarter Friday but played 41 minutes Sunday with Norman Powell and Caleb Wilson out, and he finished the overtime game. Chicago is on the second night of a back-to-back against Cleveland, which is without Evan Mobley.
notes.Jalen Smith: Smith played through an illness tag and started Sunday for 34 minutes with Nic Claxton out sick. Chicago had not filed today's report this morning, so Claxton's status for the back-to-back is not posted.
notes.Bennett Stirtz: Stirtz played 32 minutes off the bench Sunday and closed the game because Oklahoma City had only nine players with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander out. The Thunder had not filed today's report this morning, so how many guards are available at Indiana is not posted.
notes.Josh Dix: Dix played 32 minutes off the bench Sunday and closed the game with Oklahoma City down to nine players. His minutes depend on whether Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the other injured guards return, and the Thunder have not filed today's report.
notes.Svi Mykhailiuk: Mykhailiuk has played 28 to 34 bench minutes in each of his last four games because Utah is missing Lauri Markkanen, Jusuf Nurkic and Jaren Jackson Jr. Utah is on the second night of a back-to-back at the Lakers and had not filed today's report this morning.
notes.Mo Bamba: Bamba played 23 minutes Sunday after Jaxson Hayes left with a knee injury in the second quarter, and Hayes is questionable tonight at the Lakers. With Jusuf Nurkic and Jaren Jackson Jr. also out, Bamba is Utah's next center up if Hayes sits.
notes.Collin Murray-Boyles: Murray-Boyles is probable to return from the concussion protocol against Milwaukee after missing Friday. Before the injury he had taken Toronto's starting center job, playing 33 to 40 minutes in his last two full games.
notes.Luka Doncic: Austin Reaves is out again, which puts more of the Lakers' offense on Doncic against a Utah team on the second night of a back-to-back that played Sunday without Lauri Markkanen, Jusuf Nurkic and Jaren Jackson Jr. The 13.5-point spread brings some blowout risk to his minutes.
notes.Matisse Thybulle: Thybulle has started every Lakers game in a defensive role and has not played fewer than 21 minutes since November 4, and Austin Reaves is out again tonight. His value comes from steals and blocks, not scoring.
